text:
Toronto trailed 3-0 early in the second period and still won in overtime, and the way it got there says more about the first period than the last two. Nashville took 2.52 expected goals to Toronto's 1.02 in the opening 20 minutes, with Steven Stamkos scoring on the power play and Nils Hoglander adding two backhanders (the second came after a stretch of play where the Predators looked like the only team in the building). Hoglander's second goal made it 3-0 at 3:03 of the period, though it was a low-quality chance at 29 percent.

From there the game turned completely. Toronto outscored Nashville 5-1 the rest of the way and outplayed it in every remaining period, out-chancing the Predators 1.41 to 0.88 in the second and 1.01 to 0.27 in the third. John Tavares scored on a 4 percent chance, William Nylander cashed in on the power play, and Gavin McKenna scored his own goal after Stamkos had restored the two-goal lead at 4-2. Jack Roslovic tied it in the third, and Auston Matthews finished it in overtime on an assist from Nylander. Matthews had three assists as well, and his line drove 2.67 expected goals against just 0.78 allowed.

Toronto's 72 shot attempts to 52 and 4.42 expected goals to 4.01 earned it a 56 percent claim to deserving the win, so the result was fair even if the opening was not. Anthony Stolarz stopped what a goalie would be expected to stop, while Juuse Saros allowed about half a goal more than expected. Toronto also won 64 percent of faceoffs, which helped it hold the puck once it found its footing.
